title: DAB Staining of FFPE Slides
author: Jerelyn Nick
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdiei4be
materials: Primary antibody incubation Prepare desired dilutions of primary antibody in Antibody Diluent (Thermo Fisher)
Immerse slide holder into water for 1 minute.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and rehydrate slides
steps.instruction: Place slides in a xylene‑compatible rack and run the following sequential immersions:

substeps.instruction: First xylene bath – 5 min
Second xylene bath – 5 min
First 100 % ethanol – 5 min
Second 100 % ethanol – 5 min
95 % ethanol – 5 min
75 % ethanol – 5 min
50 % ethanol – 5 min
Deionized water – 5 min
Second deionized water – 5 min

steps.title: Block endogenous peroxidase
steps.instruction: Transfer the slide holder into freshly prepared 3 % H₂O₂ in methanol for 10 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 3 % H₂O₂ solution daily: mix 25 mL 30 % H₂O₂ with 225 mL methanol.

steps.title: Heat‑mediated antigen retrieval
steps.instruction: Perform citrate‑buffer antigen retrieval using microwave heating and bench incubation.

substeps.instruction: Place slides in a Coplin jar containing 10 mM pH 6.0 sodium citrate buffer (buffer level must be above the slide tops).
Place the Coplin jar inside a 400 mL beaker filled with water, leaving ~1 cm space between water level and the jar cap; keep the cap loosely held in place.
Microwave the assembly for 7 min at 50 % power.
Incubate the slides on the benchtop in the citrate buffer for an additional 18 min.
Prepare 1X TBST for later use: 90 mL deionized water, 10 mL 10X TBS (pH 7.6), 1 mL 10 % Tween‑20.

steps.title: Post‑retrieval washes
steps.instruction: Wash slides sequentially to remove citrate buffer and re‑equilibrate.

substeps.instruction: 95 % ethanol – 5 min
75 % ethanol – 5 min
50 % ethanol – 5 min
Deionized water – 5 min
Second deionized water – 5 min
Remove slides one at a time from the Coplin jar and dip in deionized water to remove residual citrate buffer.
Prepare avidin solution: 1 mL 1X TBST + 6 drops avidin (Vector Avidin‑Biotin kit).
Tap off excess buffer from slides, cover sections with avidin solution, and incubate 20 min in a humidity chamber at room temperature.

steps.title: Biotin block
steps.instruction: Block remaining endogenous biotin with biotin.

substeps.instruction: Prepare biotin solution: 1 mL 1X TBST + 6 drops biotin (Vector kit).
Tap off avidin solution, cover sections with biotin solution, and incubate 20 min in a humidity chamber.

steps.title: Serum block
steps.instruction: Block non‑specific protein binding with serum.

substeps.instruction: Prepare serum block: 1 mL 1X TBST + 20 µL normal serum from the same species as the biotinylated secondary antibody.
Tap off biotin solution, briefly rinse with 1X TBST, remove excess moisture with gauze, cover sections with serum block, and incubate 60 min in a humidity chamber.
Remove excess serum with gauze.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Apply primary antibody and incubate overnight.

substeps.instruction: Remove the humidity chamber, lift slides, discard any plastic bag coverslips, and wash slides with 1X TBST for 5 min at room temperature.
Apply primary antibody solution directly onto each section, cover with a clean plastic slip, place back into a humidity chamber, and incubate overnight (≈16–18 h) at 4 °C.
Prepare secondary solution: 1 mL 1X TBST + 15 µL species‑matched serum + 5 µL Vector biotinylated secondary antibody (directed against the primary antibody species).
After primary incubation, tip off buffer, remove excess moisture with gauze, cover sections with secondary solution, and incubate 30 min at room temperature in a humidity chamber.
Tip off buffer, remove excess moisture with gauze, and wash slides in 1X TBST for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: ABC reagent incubation
steps.instruction: Apply ABC complex for signal amplification.

substeps.instruction: Prepare ABC reagent at least 30 min before use: mix 20 µL reagent A with 1 mL 1X TBST, then add 20 µL reagent B and mix.
Cover sections with ABC reagent and incubate 30 min at room temperature in a humidity chamber.
Wash slides in 1X TBST for 5 min at room temperature. Slides may be kept in buffer until DAB staining.

steps.title: DAB development
steps.instruction: Develop chromogen to visualize antibody binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DAB solution: 1 drop DAB + 1 mL Immpact Diluent.
Cover sections with DAB solution and incubate until the desired brown intensity is reached (monitor under microscope).
Rinse slides and keep them in water until counterstaining. Collect DAB waste as hazardous chemical.
Place slides in a humidity chamber, immediately cover sections with 1X TBST, and equilibrate for 5 min.
Remove slides from water and place them into a xylene‑compatible holder.
Dip holder into hematoxylin for 10 seconds.
Rinse in running tap water until the water runs clear.

steps.title: Bluing and clarification
steps.instruction: Convert hematoxylin to blue and clarify tissue.

substeps.instruction: Immerse holder in Clarifier for 20 seconds.
Immerse holder in Bluing Reagent for 1 minute.

steps.title: Dehydrate for mounting
steps.instruction: Pass slides through graded ethanol and xylene before coverslip.

substeps.instruction: 50 % ethanol – 5 min
75 % ethanol – 5 min
95 % ethanol – 5 min
100 % ethanol – 5 min
Second 100 % ethanol – 5 min (total 10 min)
First xylene – 3 min
Second xylene – 3 min

steps.title: Mount coverslip
steps.instruction: Apply permanent mounting medium and coverslip.

substeps.instruction: In a fume hood, remove slides from xylene one side at a time.
Place approximately 2 drops of Shandon Mountant on the slide, lay a coverslip, and blot excess mountant with a paper towel.
Allow the slide to dry in the fume hood.

steps.title: Image slides
steps.instruction: Acquire bright‑field images; antibody staining appears brown and nuclei appear light blue.
